It's hard to believe it's been almost 4 years since I wrote this article.

This was the introduction:

"I am not being hyperbolic. I truly believe that we are at the precipice of a world-changing paradigm being ushered in by the advent of accessible AI.

I also believe that virtually everyone on earth is either unaware, or is underestimating the impact this is going to have on our lives.

The closest thing I can think to relate this to is the impact that the internet had on humanity.

AI is going to be even more disruptive.

My goal in writing this Letter is to open people’s eyes. To help you (and to help myself, through researching) better understand what is happening, and to attempt to understand what is likely to happen.

To help prepare ourselves for an impossible-to-prepare-for future.

Our perception of reality is going to forever shift.

We’re going to bring people back from the dead.

Almost every currently conceivable job will be doable by AI in the future (note that I said will be doable, not will be done).

There’s a lot to be afraid of. 

There’s also a lot to be excited by."

We were on the precipice then, we are on the VERY EDGE OF THE PRECIPICE now.

No idea what the next few years are going to bring, but I still very much feel that life as we know it is over. 

Hopefully in a good way.

Philip Fisher wrote in Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits that the best companies sometimes deliberately spend heavily on future growth (research, expansion, new business lines) in ways that temporarily crush near-term earnings or cash flow.

He saw this as a feature, not a bug, provided the spending was genuine investment for the future and management had a long-range outlook.

Today’s market is doing the opposite. It is punishing Amazon, Google and Meta for turning free cash flow negative while they spend aggressively on AI infrastructure, even as these companies say this spend is a must and 2027 capex will be higher.

Fisher would have recognized this. The short-term cash burn is the cost of building capacity the companies believe will generate returns for years. The market is focused on the bill, best to focus on the opportunity.
